text: You lose your whole order when your waiter goes home.
That is how MCP worked until July twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six.
MCP is how AI apps reach their tools.
An app first shook hands with one server, and could be given a session ID, like a table number.
Only that server knew the order.
On a busy night, the others could not simply step in.
The MCP specification that shipped that day removes both.
Every request is now a complete order slip, so any server can take it.
Need something remembered, like a shopping basket?
The server hands back a ticket, and the app shows it next time.
So a busy restaurant just adds servers.
Any request can land on any of them.
And if one goes home, the next one takes your order.
The fix was never a better waiter.
It was moving the memory out of his head and onto the slip.
A server that remembers nothing is a server anyone can replace.
